Classification guard: both authored edges assert association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly:true). They record that venous thromboembolism occurs after total hip and knee arthroplasty at a quantified cumulative incidence despite routine prophylaxis, and that post-arthroplasty stiffness is attributed to soft-tissue contracture, not that the arthroplasty caused either outcome in any individual; the located evidence mixes prophylaxis-comparison cohorts with small revision series, so individual claims require procedure and prophylaxis documentation with dates, outcome-specific measures, and exclusion of the competing mechanisms listed on each edge.

governanceNotes: D1 batch 49 (2026-09-24): two bounded association edges authored - joint replacement residuals to deep-vein-thrombosis (rank 1) and to contractures (rank 2), both ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true; mechanismCategory THROMBOTIC_OR_VASCULAR for the thromboembolic window (surgical venous stasis, endothelial injury, and postoperative hypercoagulability) and POST_SURGICAL_OR_TREATMENT for the stiffness window (post-arthroplasty scar-tissue formation and soft-tissue contracture). The thromboembolic proposition rests on the Simon 2023 retrospective cohort of 29,264 patients undergoing hip or knee arthroplasty drawn from a large claims database, which reported a 30-day cumulative incidence of post-discharge venous thromboembolism of 1.19% (95% CI 1.06-1.32%) alongside a 3.43% bleeding incidence and identified prior venous thromboembolism, hereditary hypercoagulable state, knee arthroplasty, and male sex as leading risk factors, and on the Lieberman 2021 review of venous thromboembolic prophylaxis after total hip and knee arthroplasty, which records that prophylaxis selection balances efficacy against bleeding, that American College of Chest Physicians guidelines recommend at least 10 to 14 days of prophylaxis after these procedures, and that validated risk stratification is essential - the quantified incidence and guideline-level anchors. The stiffness proposition rests on the Ries and Badalamente series of six total knee arthroplasties in five patients revised for persistent limited motion, in which no cause of stiffness was identified other than soft-tissue contracture, heterotopic bone was present in two knees before and five after revision, and the arc of motion improved from a mean 36 degrees to 86 degrees after revision, and on the Bong and Di Cesare review of stiffness after total knee arthroplasty, which sets out the mobilization, manipulation, lysis, and revision algorithm and the timing considerations for each. Neither edge is raised to causation: the thromboembolic cohort is a claims-based prophylaxis-comparison study with residual confounding and the stiffness evidence is a small revision series plus a treatment review.

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) prophylaxis context - the thromboembolic incidence of 1.19% was measured in patients already receiving pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, so the risk is treatment-modified rather than the untreated natural history, and the same cohort found bleeding in 3.43% of patients, which is why no comparative or superiority claim about agents is made; (ii) multifactorial stiffness - the located series found contracture as the identified cause of stiffness but also recorded heterotopic bone in seven of eleven knee observations, and the review notes intrinsic and extrinsic causes including malpositioned or oversize components, so the contracture window is bounded and does not attribute every stiff arthroplasty to soft-tissue contracture; (iii) timing - the thromboembolic outcome is quantified at 30 days post-operatively while the stiffness literature concerns presentations beyond three months, so each edge carries its own chronology requirement rather than a single window.

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) no pulmonary-embolism edge - the deep-vein-thrombosis identity already authors that downstream window (intermediate-chain guard); (ii) no peripheral-nerve-paralysis, femoral-neuropathy, or sciatic-nerve edge - no condition-specific post-arthroplasty nerve-palsy quantification was retrieved in this batch window and those windows belong to their own primaries (zero-record and duplicate-scope guards); (iii) no osteomyelitis, abscesses, cellulitis, or prosthetic-joint-infection edge - no prosthetic-joint-infection identity exists, and the located literature addresses thrombosis and stiffness rather than infection (wrong-target and zero-record guards); (iv) no unexplained-chronic-pain edge - the located stiffness evidence measures range of motion rather than persistent pain as a distinct outcome in this window, and the pain windows belong to their own primaries (zero-record guard); (v) no heterotopic-ossification edge - heterotopic bone was an incidental finding in the stiffness series rather than a quantified post-arthroplasty outcome, and that identity authors its own windows (zero-record and duplicate-scope guards); (vi) no depressive-disorder, insomnia, or anxiety-disorder edge - no condition-specific post-arthroplasty psychosocial quantification was located (zero-record guard); (vii) no scars, muscle-atrophy, or loss-of-use-of-extremities edge - no condition-specific data were located and those identities belong to their own primaries (zero-record guards); (viii) duplicate-scope note: this batch adds the first joint-replacement-residuals-primary windows to the registry.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Clinical cohorts and guideline reviews document venous thromboembolism after total hip and knee arthroplasty: the Simon 2023 retrospective cohort of 29,264 arthroplasty patients reported a 30-day cumulative incidence of post-discharge venous thromboembolism of 1.19% (95% CI 1.06-1.32%) with knee arthroplasty, prior venous thromboembolism, and hereditary hypercoagulable state among the leading risk factors, and the Lieberman 2021 review records that American College of Chest Physicians guidelines recommend at least 10 to 14 days of thromboprophylaxis after these procedures and that risk stratification is essential to balance thrombosis against bleeding - a reproducible co-occurrence association rather than an individual causal nexus.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established: the located cohort is a claims-based study of prophylaxis strategies rather than an untreated natural-history cohort, the measured incidence of 1.19% was observed in patients already receiving pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, and the same study recorded bleeding in 3.43%, so the postoperative risk is treatment-modified and influenced by patient-level thrombophilia, prior venous thromboembolism, procedure type, and mobilization; an individual determination therefore requires the operative and prophylaxis records with dates, imaging confirmation of the thrombosis, symptom chronology, and exclusion of the competing causes listed on this edge.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized thrombotic route is described: major joint arthroplasty engages all three elements of the thrombotic triad - intra-operative and postoperative venous stasis from immobility and limb positioning, endothelial and intimal injury from the surgical approach, instrumentation, and cement or tourniquet effects, and postoperative hypercoagulability from surgical inflammation and reduced fibrinolysis - so a deep venous thrombus can form in the operated limb, which is why routine pharmacologic prophylaxis for at least 10 to 14 days is recommended and why the located cohort still measured a 30-day cumulative incidence of 1.19% despite prophylaxis; the claims-based design and the patient-level risk factors leave individual attribution hypothesized.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Patient-level thrombophilia, prior venous thromboembolism, obesity, malignancy, hormone therapy, and delayed mobilization independently increase risk, and bilateral or revision procedures and prolonged operative times add to the stasis and injury burden.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The edge asserts an association only: a 29,264-patient cohort measured a 30-day post-arthroplasty venous thromboembolism incidence of 1.19% and a guideline review documents routine prophylaxis after total hip and knee arthroplasty, but the cohort is claims-based and prophylaxis-treated, the risk is modified by patient-level thrombophilia and prior events, and no untreated natural-history comparison exists, so no at-least-as-likely-as-not probability is asserted and an individual claim requires operative and prophylaxis documentation, imaging confirmation, chronology, and exclusion of competing causes.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Operative documentation (date, joint, primary or revision procedure, anaesthetic type, tourniquet use, cemented or cementless fixation, operative duration, and intra-operative complications); the thromboprophylaxis regimen actually received with agent, dose, start and stop dates, and any interruption or non-adherence; imaging confirmation of the thrombosis (venous duplex ultrasound, computed tomography venography, or venography) with the date and the vessel involved; symptom onset and chronology relative to the operation; documentation of prior venous thromboembolism, known thrombophilia, active malignancy, obesity, hormone or anticoagulant therapy, and mobility status at the time of the event; assessment of competing causes including immobility unrelated to the surgery, malignancy, inherited or acquired thrombophilia, central venous catheter thrombosis, and superficial thrombophlebitis; orthopaedic, haematology, or vascular assessment of whether the arthroplasty and its postoperative course materially contributed to the thrombosis
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Inherited or acquired thrombophilia and prior venous thromboembolism
Immobility, prolonged travel, or paralysis unrelated to the arthroplasty
Central venous catheter or device-related thrombosis
Superficial thrombophlebitis or muscle-vein thrombosis rather than deep venous thrombosis

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: a retrospective cohort of 29,264 hip and knee arthroplasty patients reported a 30-day cumulative incidence of post-discharge venous thromboembolism of 1.19% (95% CI 1.06-1.32%), and a guideline-based review records that at least 10 to 14 days of thromboprophylaxis is recommended after these procedures, establishing a reproducible co-occurrence association; the edge is not raised to causation because the cohort is claims-based and measured risk in prophylaxis-treated patients, patient-level thrombophilia and prior events modify the risk, and no untreated comparison exists, so the consensus remains NOT_ESTABLISHED with operative, prophylaxis, imaging, chronology, and competing-cause requirements and no probability estimate is asserted.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Clinical series and reviews document post-arthroplasty joint stiffness attributed to soft-tissue contracture: the Ries and Badalamente series of six total knee arthroplasties in five patients revised for persistent limited motion found no cause of stiffness other than soft tissue contracture, with arc of motion improving from a mean 36 degrees to 86 degrees after revision, and the Bong and Di Cesare review of stiffness after total knee arthroplasty sets out the physical therapy, manipulation, lysis of adhesions, and revision algorithm with its timing and identifies intrinsic and extrinsic causes including component malposition - a reproducible co-occurrence association rather than an individual causal nexus.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established: the located series is a small revision cohort without a denominator for the arthroplasty population, heterotopic bone was recorded in seven of the eleven knee observations, and the review notes that stiffness may arise from malpositioned or oversize components, inadequate rehabilitation, infection, or patient predisposition rather than from soft-tissue contracture alone; an individual determination therefore requires operative records and implant position documentation, serial range-of-motion measurements with dates, imaging and inflammatory-marker evaluation for infection and heterotopic bone, and exclusion of the competing mechanisms listed on this edge.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized post-surgical route is described: arthrotomy and soft-tissue dissection together with the inflammatory and fibrotic healing response after arthroplasty can produce extensive scar-tissue formation and soft-tissue contracture, which restricts the arc of motion - the mechanism recorded in the Ries and Badalamente series, in which no cause of stiffness was identified in six revised knees other than soft tissue contracture and the arc of motion improved from a mean 36 degrees to 86 degrees after revision, and treated in the Bong and Di Cesare algorithm through mobilization, manipulation, arthroscopic or open lysis of adhesions, and revision arthroplasty; the small uncontrolled series and the coexisting heterotopic bone and component-position contributors leave individual attribution hypothesized.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Component malposition or oversize, inadequate or delayed rehabilitation, prolonged immobilisation, arthrofibrosis predisposition, infection, and heterotopic ossification can each produce or maintain restricted motion independently of the soft-tissue contracture.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The edge asserts an association only: a six-knee revision series identified soft-tissue contracture as the cause of post-arthroplasty stiffness and a treatment review documents the clinical algorithm, but the series is small and uncontrolled with coexisting heterotopic bone in most observations, and component malposition, infection, and rehabilitation factors are competing causes, so no at-least-as-likely-as-not probability is asserted and an individual claim requires operative and implant-position documentation, serial range-of-motion measurements, infection and heterotopic-ossification evaluation, and competing-cause exclusion.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Operative documentation (date, joint replaced, primary or revision procedure, implant type and position, patellar resurfacing, alignment, and intra-operative findings) and the postoperative rehabilitation programme with its timing and adherence; serial range-of-motion measurements with dates (active and passive flexion and extension, and any fixed flexion deformity) including the best range achieved after surgery; imaging (radiographs and where performed computed tomography) documenting component position, loosening, and heterotopic bone with dates; evaluation for infection including erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein, and synovial fluid analysis where performed; assessment of competing causes including malposition or oversize, infection, heterotopic ossification, complex regional pain syndrome, patellar complications, and inadequate rehabilitation; orthopaedic assessment of whether the arthroplasty and soft-tissue healing materially contributed to the contracted range of motion
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Component malposition, oversize, or malrotation and polyethylene wear
Complex regional pain syndrome or other neuropathic pain limiting motion
Inadequate or delayed rehabilitation and pre-existing restricted motion

evidenceGaps: Operative documentation (date, joint replaced, primary or revision procedure, implant type and position, patellar resurfacing, alignment, and intra-operative findings) and the postoperative rehabilitation programme with its timing and adherence; serial range-of-motion measurements with dates (active and passive flexion and extension, and any fixed flexion deformity) including the best range achieved after surgery; imaging (radiographs and where performed computed tomography) documenting component position, loosening, and heterotopic bone with dates; evaluation for infection including erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein, and synovial fluid analysis where performed; assessment of competing causes including malposition or oversize, infection, heterotopic ossification, complex regional pain syndrome, patellar complications, and inadequate rehabilitation; orthopaedic assessment of whether the arthroplasty and soft-tissue healing materially contributed to the contracted range of motion
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: a series of six total knee arthroplasties in five patients revised for persistent limited motion found no cause of stiffness other than soft tissue contracture and documented improvement from a mean 36 degrees to 86 degrees of motion after revision, and a review of stiffness after total knee arthroplasty documents the management algorithm and the intrinsic and extrinsic causes, establishing a reproducible co-occurrence association between arthroplasty and restricted motion attributed to contracture; the edge is not raised to causation because the series is small and uncontrolled with heterotopic bone in most observations and because component malposition, infection, and rehabilitation factors compete, so the consensus remains NOT_ESTABLISHED with operative, motion-measurement, imaging, infection-evaluation, and competing-cause requirements and no probability estimate is asserted.
